2. The case of the appellants, in brief, is that the predecessors of the appellants filed Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1981 under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Patiya, Chittagong, praying for pre-emption of the case land. Subsequently, the said case was transferred to the Court of Munsif, Anowara, Chittagong and was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1983. That One Abeda Khatun was the original recorded tenant of the case land who used to cultivate the same through bargader and the petitioner is a contiguous land owner of the south plots of the case schedule land and on 04.10.1981, the petitioner found that respondent No.1 inspecting the schedule land and inquiring about the boundary thereof from bargader and on query the bargader with much hesitation disclosed that the respondent Nos. 1-3 purchased the same and thereafter the petitioner made search in Anowara Sub-registry Office to find out the kabala but failed to locate it and thereafter ultimately located the same in the District Registrar Office, Chittagong and got the certified copy of the sale deed dated 05.05.1980 and 29.10.1981 and the petitioner alleged that the vendor and vendee collusively created it in the District Registrar Officer to keep secrecy to avoid pre-emption and no local person has been cited as witness of the deed to maintain secrecy and that no notice of sale was given to the petitioner. 

 Lastly it is argued that neither the trial Court nor the High Court Division while dismissing the pre-emption case could show from evidence or from any other materials on record that the pre-emptor-petitioner had knowledge of the transaction before 04.10.1981 as stated by the pre-emptors." 

 5. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Counsel, appearing for the appellants submits that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that the Court of appeal below being the last Court of facts decided the issue of limitation a proper reappraisal of the, evidence and materials on record giving definite findings regarding date of knowledge of sale, while interfering with such decision in revisional jurisdiction. Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that the High Court Division was in an error of facts in not holding that in order to maintain secrecy of the sale no notice was served upon the co-sharers and the deed was registered in the District Registrar Officer leaving the local Sub-registrar Office and no person of the locality was cited as a witness of the sale deed and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. Lastly, Mr. Bhuiyan submits that the High Court Division was not proper and justified in dismissing pre-emption because neither the trial Court nor the High Court Division while dismissing the pre-emption case could show from evidence or from any other materials on record that the pre-emptor had knowledge of sale before 04.10.1981 as stated by the pre-emptor and hence the impugned judgment and order as is liable to be set aside.
